page_title: KNXBench — Your KNX project. Your workbench.
description: Import KNX projects, edit your installation and see what the bus is saying. Meet KNXBench: an independent engineering app, in your browser via Docker or natively on Linux.
preview_note: Local design preview · Not published yet
alpha_tag: Independent KNX engineering app · Alpha pre-release
hero_lede: Import projects. Work with devices and group addresses. See what the bus is saying. KNXBench brings your installation into a modern engineering workspace.
platforms: In your browser via Docker. Or natively on Linux.
hero_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the fictional Sample house’s group-address tree with Kitchen light selected and its links in Properties.
strip_three: Project data with clear import reports
features_title:
From a project file
to a clear picture.
features_intro: You know your installation. Your tools should help you understand it, not get in the way. These are the highlights KNXBench puts on your workbench.
watch_title:
Don’t just read about it.
See it.
watch_intro: Short looks at the real application. Every recording uses fictional sample data, not somebody’s actual installation.
project_body: Add a device from the product catalog, assign a free address and link a communication object to a group address. Without jumping between five different tools.
project_transcript: A push button is picked from the product catalog, named “Push button dining” and created with a free individual address in the sample house. Its first communication object is then linked to 0/0/2 “Kitchen light” with the searchable address picker. The recording uses zoom and plays at double speed.
project_caption: Real app · Sample house · Zoom, 2× speed
flow_body: The flow view brings senders, receivers and values together. Here it follows lights, blinds and temperature in the sample house, in the optional green CRT theme.
flow_transcript: Simulated telegrams from the fictional sample house make devices appear in the flow view: lights switch on and off, a blind moves down, and temperature and valve values change.
details_body: Filter group addresses, select an address and inspect its properties right beside it. A calm workspace for the details that matter.
details_transcript: The real app shows the sample house’s group addresses. Typing “Kitchen” into the filter narrows the tree; 0/0/2 is selected and its properties and links appear right beside it. The filter is then cleared again.
video_fallback: Your browser cannot play this video.
personality_body: There are calm interfaces for focused work: Porcelain, Graphite and Cupertino. And, when you feel like it, green phosphor and a small starship bridge. English and German, plus Bavarian and Klingon packs for the brave, and optional achievements, because engineering work deserves a little applause.
crt_alt: The real group address table in the optional green CRT theme with fictional sample data.
crt_caption: A little phosphor on your workbench.
lcars_alt: The real KNXBench workbench in the optional LCARS theme with fictional sample data.
optional_themes: Optional. The regular workbench stays the same. Screenshots with a fictional project.
story_title:
How an idea
became a workbench.
story_body: It began with wanting a KNX tool on Linux. Then came decisions, detours, AI assistants and rather a lot of “just one more thing”. The Evolution Story follows that path, with evidence and a slightly melancholy narrator.
status_title:
Already a workbench.
Still an alpha.
status_body: KNXBench is under active development. Try it, keep backups and check whether your project and devices fit the supported scope. Your feedback helps make the next version better.
status_summary: Project work, product data and bus diagnostics are at the core. Import support and device operations have explicitly documented boundaries: not every format or device has the same level of support.
scope_import: ETS project import is limited to supported formats and versions. Warnings and unsupported content are surfaced in the import report; full ETS compatibility is not promised.
scope_export: After import, you work in .knxdb. Export back to .knxproj is not provided.
scope_hardware: Commissioning and device downloads support limited, documented paths. Project editing does not mean every device can be programmed.
scope_secure: KNX Secure is not currently implemented.
backup_note: Try a copy first. Read the application’s guidance before hardware operations.
demos_title:
A project to explore.
No installation to risk.
demos_intro: Three fictional offline projects for your own KNXBench instance. Each ZIP includes a native .knxdb, the shared fictional product catalogue and an English tour with five exercises.
demos_home_summary: 32 devices, 105 group addresses. Two living floors, basement and outside areas.
demos_residential_summary: 101 devices, 339 group addresses. Six apartments, three living floors and shared areas.
demos_office_summary: 157 devices, 507 group addresses. Three floors with offices, meeting rooms and auxiliary areas.
demos_all: Download all three demos (ZIP on GitHub)
demos_setup: Extract a ZIP and keep an untouched reset copy. Install fictional-demo-devices.knxprod once through Product catalog, then open a copy of the .knxdb via File → Open. Native edits can auto-save.
demos_safety: Offline exploration only. Fictional applications contain no firmware and must never be downloaded to real devices. These projects are not ETS exports or electrical plans.
demos_version_note: Demo version 1.0.0. The frozen ZIP READMEs retain their original “local review candidate” label. See the guide for the tested development build; compatibility with older alpha releases is not promised.
start_title:
The next view
is your own.
start_body: No account with us. No hosted demo. KNXBench runs on your own instance, so you try the real product.
launch_note: The repository and its alpha downloads are public on GitHub. This website itself is still a preview and not published yet.
docker_body: Use the web app through a suitable Docker environment on your system. The container brings the interface and server together; you stay in control of your projects.
docker_step_two: Pull the ready-made image, configure storage and access.
docker_step_three: Open it in your browser, create a project or import a copy.
docker_note: Images for amd64 and arm64. Pin a version tag for a reproducible setup, or follow latest, which includes alpha releases. The guide also explains networking for live-bus access.
native_body: The Linux AppImage packages the desktop application for x86-64. Downloads and SHA-256 checksums are on the release page; read the system requirements and installation guidance before upgrading.
native_note: Choose a release, read its notes and work with project copies.
support_intro: You don’t have to figure it all out alone.
footer_tagline: An independent workbench for KNX projects.
independence: KNXBench is an independent project. It is not affiliated with the KNX Association and is not KNX certified. KNX and ETS are mentioned to describe the application’s scope.
license_note: Free software under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Free to use, including commercially, subject to the licence terms.
privacy_body: This website uses no analytics scripts, marketing cookies, embedded video services or remotely hosted fonts. Media and fonts load from the same site host. GitHub links lead to an external service.
privacy_pending: Before public launch, information about the actual hosting, possible server logs and privacy enquiries will be added and reviewed. This local preview is not a final privacy notice for the future site.
contact_body: Public project feedback and support gaps can be reported on GitHub in the KNXBench repository, using its support-gap form. Share only information explicitly approved for public disclosure, not confidential projects or credentials.
privacy_hosting: This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. According to GitHub's documentation, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes when a GitHub Pages site is visited. For privacy enquiries, use the contact on the legal notice page.
hl_import_body: Open a .knxproj from ETS and KNXBench assembles the whole picture: topology, buildings, devices, group addresses and their links. The import report names every warning and everything it could not model, instead of quietly dropping it, and unknown source data is preserved wherever possible. From there you continue in KNXBench’s own versioned project format, or you simply start a fresh project.
hl_import_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the project status page of the fictional Sample house right after its import, with project contents and the import report.
hl_history_body: Every edit is a validated step you can undo and redo, from a renamed group address to a freshly linked object. Before a big change, give the project a named version and find it again later on the history timeline. The whole project lives in one versioned .knxdb file that migrates forward safely, and a file from the future is refused rather than guessed at.
hl_history_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the Project history dialog of the fictional Sample house with the named version Before the kitchen redesign.
hl_wizard_body: The new-project wizard sets up areas, lines, rooms and group ranges in one go. The add-device wizard takes a product from the catalogue, places it on a line and lets the server preview names and free individual addresses before anything is created. Check the review, confirm, done. No surprises, no address collisions.
hl_wizard_note: New project · Add device · Preview first
hl_wizard_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the review step of the Add device wizard, announcing that one device, Dining room actuator, will be created with the free address 1.1.3.
hl_params_body: Every device gets a parameter workspace built from its own product data: an area register, compact aligned rows and one search across all areas. Jump between channels as often as you like; drafts and conflicts stay exactly where you left them. Long parameter lists finally feel like a form, not like a maze.
hl_params_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the Parameters tab of the fictional ground-floor switch actuator with its area register, a channel open and aligned parameter rows.
hl_catalog_body: Install manufacturer product packages, or use the product data that already ships inside your projects. Hand over a manufacturer’s ZIP and every package inside is previewed first, then installed together, or not at all. The catalogue is backed up before each installation, and manuals are listed, not hoarded. In a test run over 853 public manufacturer downloads, 852 installed.
hl_catalog_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the catalogue update of a vendor ZIP holding the fictional demo package, previewed with one package, nine programs and nine added products; nothing is installed until the backup-and-install confirmation.
hl_search_body: Press Ctrl+K and start typing: devices, group addresses and the rest of the project answer as you type. The command palette reaches every action, while the project explorer, the properties inspector and drag and drop take care of the rest. The mouse is welcome, it just isn’t mandatory.
hl_search_alt: KNXBench in Graphite: the Ctrl+K search with the query light, listing the matching group addresses of the fictional Sample house.
hl_bus_body: Discover KNXnet/IP interfaces, connect by tunnelling and follow decoded telegrams in the group monitor. The flow view turns the traffic into a living map in which devices light up as they talk, and saves a PNG or a short GIF when you want to show somebody. You can send group values too, when you mean it.
hl_docs_body: Export and import group addresses as CSV, produce a self-contained HTML project document with print preview, and compare two projects value by value. The comparison also runs on the command line, with an exit code your CI will love.
hl_ai_title: An AI agent at the workbench, not on the bus.
hl_ai_body: knx-mcp lets an MCP client such as Claude Code answer questions about your saved projects: read-only by default and without any bus access. A single explicit opt-in allows a previewed and confirmed naming recipe for group addresses. Experimental, and deliberately careful.
